instructions: Read one acceptance criterion from a product spec. Choose every feature when the criterion states a rule that applies to every feature or every change of some kind across the project, such as every change to what a user sees, every new endpoint, or every stored field, whatever feature is being built. Choose this feature when the criterion describes the behavior of one feature, page, command, or component, even when it uses words like every or all inside that feature.

labels.name: every feature
labels.description: The criterion is a rule that every feature or every change of a kind must meet, across the whole project.

input.criterion: When any change adds a screen or alters what a user can do, the change ships with its help center article.
Every new API endpoint is listed in the public changelog before release.
When a feature stores a new personal data field, the privacy notice names that field.

labels.name: this feature
labels.description: The criterion describes the behavior of one feature, page, command, or component only.

input.criterion: When the invoice list has more than fifty rows, it pages them fifty at a time.
Every row of the billing table shows its due date and amount.
When the upload fails, the dialog keeps the chosen file and shows a retry button.
